verdict.line: You lose if you trade into her Q poke while her W (Hallowed Mist) is up; you win if you survive to Trinity Force and force fights once her W and E are both down.

brief.thesis: Gwen's kit is built to deny Nasus's stacking: W (Hallowed Mist) makes her untargetable to anyone who doesn't walk in, and Q (Snip Snip!) pokes the minion wave and Nasus at the same time while feeding her A Thousand Cuts sustain, so trading CS through her poke just heals her. Neither side has hard CC or a real gap-closer stun, so this isn't decided by one skirmish — it's decided by whether Nasus's Q stacks and Trinity Force spike before she runs away with lane. The 47.6% head-to-head over 1230 games reflects that: close, but tilted toward her early poke advantage.

theirWindow.what: She can Q (Snip Snip!) poke the wave and you from inside it without being punished, since only enemies who enter the mist can target her. Don't walk in to trade — let the poke land and keep farming behind minions.

yourWindow.when: Her W and E are both down
yourWindow.what: She has no dash to disengage and no mist to hide in. Land W (Wither) to decelerate her, then commit Q and E (Spirit Fire) — this is the only window where the trade is fully on your terms.

powerCurve.note: Her Q cone poke outranges your Q at rank 1
E (Skip 'n Slash) harass continues while your Q is still single-target
R (Fury of the Sands) and Wither slows even the fight
Trinity Force online, Q stacks snowball damage
Full build tanks her poke, stacks win skirmishes

start.why: The flat damage reduction on takes-damage-from-champion-attacks directly blunts her Q (Snip Snip!) poke and the true-damage center hit of A Thousand Cuts, and it's the dominant start at 63.1% pick / 47.9% WR.

boots.why: Most-picked boot at 54.2%; the ability haste shortens Wither and Spirit Fire cooldowns so you can threaten her E (Skip 'n Slash) dash window more often.

core.why: Spellblade procs punish her when she dashes in with E, and the stats scale your stacked Q damage immediately.
The attack speed slow aura cuts into the on-hit window her E grants her, making her follow-up autos whiff more.
Flat magic resist plus healing amp directly counters her all-magic-damage kit and offsets what her Q/passive chips off.

situational.when: she's leaning on A Thousand Cuts healing to win extended trades
you need the anti-heal online before Thornmail finishes
her magic burst alone is threatening to kill you in skirmishes

runes.keystoneWhy: The heal-and-move proc on energized autos sustains you through her Q poke and gives you the mobility to walk in only when her mist is down.

summoners.why: Highest measured winrate pairing at 48.8%. Teleport lets you freeze the wave and still answer ganks or return from base without losing stacking time; Ghost closes the gap on her once her E (Skip 'n Slash) dash is spent.

playing.title: Farm through Spirit Fire, not autos
playing.detail: Use E (Spirit Fire) on caster and cannon waves so you clear safely while she tries to poke the center of her Q cone. This denies her free damage without you walking into melee range.

playing.title: Punish whiffed E dashes
playing.detail: Her E (Skip 'n Slash) is a 13/12.5/12/11.5/11s cooldown dash — if she dashes and misses her follow-up attack window, she's stuck at melee range with no refund. That's your cue to Q and Wither.

playing.title: Never trade into an up W
playing.detail: If her W (Hallowed Mist) is available, assume she can go untargetable the moment you commit. Wait it out rather than forcing a fight she can escape for free.

playing.title: Lock her with Wither before committing
playing.detail: W (Wither) decelerates her movement and attack speed over time — land it before she can dash away, not after, since it does nothing to stop the initial E engage.

playing.title: Freeze near turret early
playing.detail: Levels 1-5 you're behind in trades, so hold the wave near your tower and let Spirit Fire do the last-hitting while her poke has to cross more distance to reach you.

playing.title: Save R for skirmishes, not burst
playing.detail: R (Fury of the Sands) drains nearby enemies' max health over its duration rather than nuking instantly — use it to win extended level 6+ fights, not as a quick-kill button.

playing.title: Itemize Frozen Heart before Spirit Visage if poked hard
playing.detail: If her E on-hit attack speed buff is winning extended trades, take Frozen Heart's aura earlier in the build order to blunt it before finishing Spirit Visage.

brief.patchCaveat: The build order, boots, runes, summoners, and all win-rate/pick-rate numbers above are measured from live OP.GG games on the current patch; the mechanical reasoning and timing calls are my own tactical read, not measured data.
